<xpln lang="en"><etym lang="tbd">[<term lang="du">dogghe,</term> Dutch.]</etym>
1. A domestick animal remarkably various in his species; com­
prising the mastiff, the spaniel, the buldog, the greyhound,
the hound, the terrier, the cur, with many others. The
larger sort are used as a guard; the less for sports.
<term lang="quo">Such smiling rogues as these sooth every passion:
Renege, affirm, and turn their halcyon beaks
With ev'ry gale and vary of their masters,
As knowing nought, like dogs, but following. Shak. K. Lear.</term>
<term lang="quo">Why should we not think a watch and pistol as distinct
species one from another, as a horse and a dog. Locke.</term>
<term lang="quo">The clamour roars of men and boys, and dogs,
Ere the soft fearful people, to the flood
Commit their woolly sides. Thomson's Spring, l. 375.</term>
2. A constellation called Sirius, or Canicula, rising and setting
with the sun during the canicular days, or dog days.
<term lang="quo">Among the southern constellations two there are who bear
the name of the dog; the one in sixteen degrees latitude, con­
taining on the left thigh a star of the first magnitude, usually
called Procyon, or Anticanus. Brown's Vulgar Errours, b. iv.</term>
<term lang="quo">It parts the twins and crab, the dog divides,
And Argo's keel that broke the frothy tides. Creech.</term>
3. A reproachful name for a man.
<term lang="quo">I never heard a passion so confus'd,
So strange, outrageous, and so variable,
As the dog Jew did utter in the streets. Shak. Mer. of Venice.</term>
<term lang="quo">Beware of dogs, beware of evil workers. Phil. iii. 2.</term>
4. To give or send to the DOGS; to throw away. To go to the
DOGS; to be ruined, destroyed, or devoured.
<term lang="quo">Had whole Colepeper's wealth been hops and hogs,
Could he himself have sent it to the dogs? Pope's Epistles.</term>
5. It is used as the term for the male of several species; as,
the dog fox, the dog otter.
<term lang="quo">If ever I thank any man, I'll thank you; but that they call
compliments is like the encounter of two dog apes. Shakesp.</term>
6. Dog is a particle added to any thing to mark meanness, or
degeneracy, or worthlessness; as dog rose.</xpln>

<xpln lang="en"><etym lang="tbd">[from the noun.]</etym> To hunt as a dog, insidiously
and indefatigably.
<term lang="quo">I have dogg'd him like his murtherer. Shakes. Twelfth Night.</term>
<term lang="quo">His taken labours bid him me forgive;
I, his despiteful Juno, sent him forth
From courtly friends, with camping foes to live,
Where death and danger dog the heels of worth. Shakesp.</term>
<term lang="quo">Sorrow dogging sin,
Afflictions sorted. Herbert.</term>
<term lang="quo">These spiritual joys are dogged by no such sad sequels as are
the products of those titillations, that reach no higher than
fancy and the senses. Glanv. Sceps. Pref.</term>
<term lang="quo">I have been pursued, dogged, and way-laid through several
nations, and even now scarce think myself secure. Pope.</term>
<term lang="quo">Hate dogs their rise, and insult mocks their fall.
Vanity of Human Wishes.</term></xpln>
